TheForms job isn't just writing checks.

Founders carry more than most people see — the pressure to always be "on," the isolation of making every hard call alone, the weight of expectations from investors, teams, and themselves.

As investors, we believe our role goes further than capital:

→ Creating space for founders, not just funding rounds
→ Supporting resilience, not demanding heroics
→ Being present for the hard months, not just the wins

Burnout isn't a badge of honor. It's a risk to the very thing we're all trying to build.

The founders who last aren't the ones who never rest — they're the ones who learn when to pause, ask for help, and protect their own wellbeing along the way.

Building something great shouldn't cost your health. 🤍

Three items landed on the 2026 rulemaking calendar: asset sales, custody rules, market-structure changes. This isn't noise — it's the groundwork institutions have been asking for before deploying serious capital.

Regulatory clarity has been the biggest blocker holding back large-scale institutional entry into digital assets. Every step toward defined rules removes friction from that path.

The market that survives the next cycle will be the one built on structure, not speculation.

And yet — that's where most capital goes.

We do it differently.

We don't skim whitepapers. We study the problem itself — the market, the history, the failed attempts before. By the time we deploy, we know more about the space than most founders pitching in it.

🔭 Long horizon
Five years, not five weeks. We're not optimizing for the next cycle. We're betting on what survives all of them.

Three items landed on the 2026 rulemaking calendar: asset sales, custody rules, market-structure changes. This isn't noise — it's the groundwork institutions have been asking for before deploying serious capital.

Regulatory clarity has been the biggest blocker holding back large-scale institutional entry into digital assets. Every step toward defined rules removes friction from that path.

The market that survives the next cycle will be the one built on structure, not speculation.

{"tweets":[{"type":"tweet","id":"2080719002448412773","url":"https://x.com/theformsvc/status/2080719002448412773","twitterUrl":"https://twitter.com/theformsvc/status/2080719002448412773","text":"💭 TheForms job isn't just writing checks.

Founders carry more than most people see — the pressure to always be "on," the isolation of making every hard call alone, the weight of expectations from investors, teams, and themselves.

As investors, we believe our role goes further than capital:

→ Creating space for founders, not just funding rounds
→ Supporting resilience, not demanding heroics
→ Being present for the hard months, not just the wins

Burnout isn't a badge of honor. It's a risk to the very thing we're all trying to build.

The founders who last aren't the ones who never rest — they're the ones who learn when to pause, ask for help, and protect their own wellbeing along the way.

Building something great shouldn't cost your health. 🤍

# Linktree

> Linktree is a link-in-bio tool used by 70M+ creators, brands, and businesses
to share everything they create, curate, and sell from a single URL. This file
lists publicly indexable, logged-out pages of https://linktr.ee/ that describe
the product, pricing, marketplace, help content, and company information.
Individual user profiles at https://linktr.ee/{username} are not enumerated here;
see the sitemaps referenced below for the full crawlable surface.

Linktree is operated by Linktree Pty Ltd. The core product lets users build a
mobile-friendly landing page that aggregates their social profiles, content,
products, and services behind a single URL. Paid plans (Starter, Pro, Premium)
add customization, analytics, commerce, scheduling, and AI features.

Notes for agents:

- User profile pages (`https://linktr.ee/{username}`) are public, server-rendered
HTML and are not listed in this file. They are discoverable via the sitemaps referenced
in `/robots.txt`.

- The Help Center is hosted on Intercom and is crawlable from `https://linktr.ee/help`.
- The blog is published at `https://linktr.ee/blog` and organized by category.
- The Marketplace lists third-party apps and integrations that creators can add to their Linktree.
- See also: https://linktr.ee/robots.txt and the sitemaps listed within it.

# Linktree LinkApp SDK

> Official documentation for the Linktree LinkApp SDK

## Docs

- [linkapp add](https://docs.linktr.ee/cli/add.md): Add components from the registry to your project
- [linkapp build](https://docs.linktr.ee/cli/build.md): Create an optimized production build of your LinkApp
- [linkapp deploy](https://docs.linktr.ee/cli/deploy.md): Deploy your LinkApp to Linktree
- [linkapp dev](https://docs.linktr.ee/cli/dev.md): Start the development server with live preview and hot reloading
- [linkapp login](https://docs.linktr.ee/cli/login.md): Authenticate with Linktree
- [linkapp logout](https://docs.linktr.ee/cli/logout.md): Sign out of Linktree
- [linkapp test-url-match-rules](https://docs.linktr.ee/cli/test-url-match-rules.md): Validate url_match_rules.json against a URL
- [Configuration](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/configuration.md): Configure your LinkApp with linkapp.config.ts
- [Manifest Reference](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/configuration/manifest.md): Complete reference for LinkApp manifest configuration
- [Settings Configuration](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/configuration/settings.md): Build user-facing settings forms for your LinkApp
- [URL Matching](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/configuration/url-matching.md): Auto-suggest your LinkApp when users enter matching URLs
- [Visibility & Discovery](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/configuration/visibility.md): Control how users find and access your LinkApp
- [Deployment](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/deployment.md): Deploy your LinkApp to Linktree
- [Layouts](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/layouts.md): Learn how LinkApp layouts work and how to create them
- [Settings Element Reference](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/settings-reference.md): Complete reference for all LinkApp settings element types
- [Advanced Elements](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/settings/advanced.md): Arrays, integrations, conditional display, and specialized elements
- [Location Element](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/settings/location.md): Google Places location picker for collecting place data
- [Selection Elements](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/settings/selections.md): Select, radio, and checkbox elements for choosing options
- [Text Input Elements](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/settings/text-inputs.md): Text, textarea, URL, and number input elements
- [Toggle Elements](https://docs.linktr.ee/essentials/settings/toggles.md): Switch and link behavior elements for on/off controls
- [Installation](https://docs.linktr.ee/installation.md): Build custom LinkApps for Linktree in minutes

id="dg-consent-custom-style">:host(.dg-consent-banner) .dg-app {

  }

    font-weight: 500;
  }

  .dg-slider:not(.essential-label) {
    height: 1.5rem;
    width: 2.4375rem;
    width: 2.4375rem;
  }

  .dg-slider::after {
    width: 1.125rem;
    height: 1.125rem;
  }

    margin-top: 0.25rem;
    margin-right: 0.25rem;
  }
}

  max-height: 24rem;
}

  :host(.dg-consent-banner) .dg-app {

      margin-bottom: 0;
    }

      margin-top: 0;
      margin-right: 0;
    }
  }
}

/* Compact styles on mobile only */
@media only screen and (max-width: 480px) {
  :host(.dg-consent-banner:not(.dg-modal)) .dg-app {
    --dg-default-margin-mobile: 0.5rem;

    grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr;

    & > *:not(button) {
      grid-column: 1 / span 3;
    }

    & > button:first-of-type {
      margin-right: 0;
    }

    & > button:last-of-type {
      margin-left: 0;
    }

    /* Move the language dropdown into the title */
    & div:has(> .dg-header) {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      position: relative;

      .dg-header-buttons {
        position: absolute;
        right: var(--dg-default-margin-mobile);
        top: calc(var(--dg-default-margin-mobile) / 2);

        margin-left: calc(var(--dg-default-margin-mobile) / 2);

        .language-dropdown-trigger-icon-start {
          margin-bottom: 0;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

        }

    }
  }
}

Our Founders' Story

Linktree is a tool to help you share everything you are, in one simple link – making your online content more discoverable, easier to manage and more likely to convert. Here’s where it all began.

In 2016 brothers Alex and Anthony Zaccaria and their business partner Nick Humphreys found a common pain point when running their digital agency, Bolster, managing social media accounts for their clients. Endlessly updating singular bio links felt like a waste of time, or worse, often got overlooked. Overnight, the first iteration of Linktree was live, and we haven’t looked back since!

Today, with 70M+ users worldwide, we’re helping brands, artists, publishers, agencies and influencers better control their presence online. As the internet became more fragmented, we grew Linktree’s functionality to better serve those using it and to streamline the content-sharing process.

We’re a passionate team of developers, designers, marketers and biz ops, committed to equipping content-creators with the best tools for getting their work seen. We’re headquartered in Melbourne, Australia and have offices in Sydney, San Francisco and Los Angeles.

In 2019 we were thrilled to be one of CNBC’s ‘Upstart 100’, a list of the “brightest, most intriguing, young startups promising to become the great companies of tomorrow”. In March 2020, Fast Company honored us in their ‘Most Innovative Companies of 2020’ list, placing us number four in the Social Media category. Previous honorees of the Social Media fourth place include Glossier and Reddit.

We want to empower Linkers of all kinds to carve out their own space on the Internet. Additionally, legal restrictions across Linktree’s many international markets limit what content we can or cannot allow on the platform.

You may:

  • create links to adult content as long as it is legal in your region, doesn’t advertise full service sex work, and is marked as sensitive*
  • advertise adult media that you create and sell on other platforms

You may not:

  • upload adult media (e.g. images or videos), including nudity, to your Linktree– including in your avatar, link thumbnails, background, PDFs, or Link Apps such as Store product images
  • embed social media feeds that would display adult content directly on your Linktree
  • advertise full service sex work
  • share adult content created with generative AI to impersonate another individual
  • use LinkApps, Linktree commerce features, or payment-locked links to distribute adult content. You may not collect payment or donations for adult content through Linktree

*When adding a link to your Linktree, you may find that the sensitive content label is automatically applied.

‍

Hate speech

Linktree is a place to share beliefs and ideas as long as it does not cause harm, incite hatred or violence, or discriminate against individuals and groups based on race, skin color, national origin, religious beliefs, sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or medical condition. We’re also not a platform that should be used to glorify perpetrators of hatred, violence, or discrimination either.

‍

Electoral fraud

Don’t use Linktree to impede your local/national electoral process, which includes misleading the public about where and how to participate, or about who can participate, and selling or attempting to sell your right to vote.

‍

URLs

Linktree usernames are meant for everyone– so don’t buy, sell, hoard or trade them. Don’t secure a username without the intention of using it, or with the intention to ’domain squat’, i.e. to prevent someone else from using it, or to profit from reselling it. This is illegal in some countries, and Linktree does not allow it.

‍

Illegal goods and services

Don’t use Linktree to advertise, encourage, or facilitate the sale of regulated or illegal goods, services, or activities, including (but not limited to):

  • Alcohol*
  • Controlled substances
  • Tobacco products, including e-cigarettes
  • Weapons, weapon schematics, accessories and ammunition, including firearms and real-life replicas lacking indicators that clearly denote they cannot be fired
  • Fireworks and explosives
  • Body parts (including body fluids, blood etc.) or offers of humans for sale
  • Endangered or protected species or parts of
  • Regulated plants, insects, animals
  • Offers for adoption/surrogacy
  • Counterfeit goods
  • Recalled items
  • Stolen items
  • Products offered through multi-level marketing schemes
  • Embargoed goods
  • Hazardous/toxic materials
  • ID documents
  • Personal information or mailing lists
  • Gambling, including casino and betting games**
  • Human trafficking

Any content designed to target minors must not promote any content that is inappropriate, unsafe or that exploits or exerts undue pressure on the targeted individuals.

*You may advertise the sale of alcohol with a liquor licence, but you may not sell alcohol directly through Linktree commerce links.

**Fantasy sports do not fall under this policy and may be freely shared on Linktree.

‍

Spam and fraud

Don’t use Linktree to spam or scam visitors. This includes (but isn’t limited to):

  • linking out to external sites which might collect personal information under false pretenses
  • creating a large number of accounts to advertise goods/services/domains
  • creating a large number of accounts to collect affiliate per-click funds

‍

Harassment

Don’t use Linktree to target individuals with the intention to intimidate, harass, threaten, or bully.

‍

Extremist/terrorist content

Don’t use Linktree to advertise, propagandize, praise, or collect funds for extremist groups or their activities.

‍

Child harm

Linktree has a no tolerance policy for child harm. Do not upload or link out to content that harms minors or endorses harming minors, including: child sexual abuse material, solicitation of minors, and imagery that feature underage individuals within an inappropriate context. We actively report any such cases of child endangerment or harm uploaded to or linked out from Linktree to relevant authorities, e.g. the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.

‍

Self-harm

We want Linktree to be a place where Linkers can feel safe as they discuss the journey of recovery in a healthy way, but we also want everyone to feel safe when visiting. As a result, we prohibit content that promotes or idealizes suicide, self-mutilation, or disordered eating.

If you or someone you know is in crisis, please consider reaching out for help. Organizations such as 7 Cups, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and IMAlive provide anonymous, free, and 24/7 support across many countries and languages.

‍

Shocking or violent content

Don’t use Linktree to share content intended to shock and disturb visitors such as gore, mutilation, excessive violence, or physical abuse.

‍

Copyright and trademark

You should not upload content that infringes an individual’s intellectual property rights (including copyright, trademarks, and patents). If you believe your intellectual property rights are being infringed because of content on Linktree, please reach out to us.

‍

Privacy and impersonation

Maintaining individual privacy is very important on Linktree! We don’t allow Linktree profiles that expose others’ personal identifying information (billing details, IDs, etc.) or collect identifying information (including IP addresses) without the appropriate legal basis (e.g. explicit consent). We also don’t allow profiles that expose private media (e.g. image-based sexual abuse, including that which was created with generative AI) or that impersonate other individuals or organisations.

If you collect personal information from visitors, you must ensure that you have a privacy notice that visitors can review before providing their personal data. This privacy notice must comply with all applicable privacy laws and regulations.

‍

Misinformation

Don’t use Linktree to post, share or spread misinformation or disinformation. This includes any content that jeopardises public safety, including but not limited to manipulated media, documentation, or conspiracy theories.

Examples:

  • content that is false, inaccurate, disproven, or designed to misinform others re: current events, social issues or crises
  • content intended to impede your local/national electoral process (please refer to our policy re: electoral fraud)
  • content that was created with the use of generative AI in an attempt to impersonate, harass, sexualize (e.g. “deepfakes”), or misinform with the intent to harm
  • content suggesting potentially harmful alternatives to medical treatment
    claims that falsely exaggerate or trivialise the effects of or origin of medical conditions or their scientifically-backed treatments, including in relation to COVID-19

‍

Grow your career at Linktree.

At Linktree, we’re empowering everyone with the tools to curate and grow their digital universe. We bet you’ve got some ideas.

See open roles

Life at Linktree

The team at Linktree is a thriving community spread across Australia, Brazil, EU, Philippines, and the US. We spend our days tackling fun technical challenges, building interactive tools, forming partnerships and teasing out unique insights; everything it takes to empower our base of 70M+ Linkers to keep selling, sharing, growing and linking limitlessly.

Thrive, your way

Staying healthy, inspired and motivated to bring your full self to work is something that we think everyone deserves. Linktree’s industry-leading approach to benefits puts you in the driver’s seat to shape a life where you can flourish (at and away from your laptop).

Flex Benefit

Nobody knows you better than you. That’s why every Linktree employee gets $7,000 AUD / $4,900 USD to spend on their wellness, growth, lifestyle, and on social impact. From gym memberships to courses, childcare, pet insurance, and green energy initiatives: the benefits that fuel your inspiration and keep you coming to work in tip top shape are yours to define.

Leave for whatever life brings

Our 18-week parental leave policy for birthing and non-birthing parents is designed to help enable everyone at Linktree to support their families and ease the transition back to work, including a return experience program offering backup childcare support, a stipend for expenses like expressing devices, and more. We’re also committed to providing time for our people experiencing pregnancy loss or other hardships that could benefit from being with loved ones and finding the support they need.

Transpositive Inclusion Policy

All of our inclusion policies are built closely in partnership with community members. Our Transpositive Inclusion Policy begins with gender inclusion training for all Linktree employees. Our trans and gender diverse employees have access to a mental health support stipend, and for those on a gender affirmation journey, we provide both financial support and leave for your consultations and procedures.

Mental health and wellbeing support

In addition to our flex benefit that can be used on wellness perks like gym memberships or massages, we also provide access to tailored counseling through Mindfit and subscription to Calm. We understand that some days you just need to switch off, so we also offer 10 mental health days to help you reinvigorate your mind and get back on track.

Flexible and asynchronous workplace

We primarily operate out of Australia, London and the US, with offices in Melbourne, LA and SF. Given our team’s distribution across multiple time zones, we’ve embraced remote and flexible work from the start, valuing collaboration above all. So depending on team and location, Linkies work either fully remote or a flex hybrid approach. We’re piloting a new program called ‘Linkie Leaps’ where teams meet in-person for days of collaboration and team-bonding.

Our commitment to social impact

This commitment starts with the individual: we offer 20 hours of volunteering and mentorship leave for every team member to support causes they care about. We commit 1% of all revenue to support social good causes and initiatives. To date, we’ve gifted 5,500+ lifetime Pro plans to nonprofits incl. Greenpeace, Planned Parenthood, UN Refugee Agency and 1 Million Women.

A workplace that lets you know you belong

At Linktree, you’re part of an empathetic, vibrant and globally-minded culture where your voice always matters. As we scale, we meet challenges and grow together, connected by how much we care about the meaningful work we do. Through training, workshops, events, community, support and inclusion policies, we foster a culture that appreciates each human in it for exactly who they are.

How we make the magic happen

We all bring something different to the table (and we wouldn’t have it any other way). Here are the values that we operate with to find the right path forward together.

Go further together

We champion collaboration, drawing from our collective strength.

Defy the ordinary

Our individual roles are different, but we’re here to do the best work of our lives.

Act then adapt

We take big leaps forward through thoughtful risks. We jump in, make tracks and course-correct as we’re moving.

Own your part

If we see something that needs fixing, we speak up, fix it and follow through.

Let curiosity lead

We believe in the wide-eyed wonder that drives us to new discoveries. We never stop learning, so we never stop growing.

Pursue deliberate simplicity

We seek clarity in the complex.
